posts.author: karthi
posts.text:
Good morning all, and welcome to FY2027/7, our 44th term 🎉 Sharing Robert's budget memo. Headline numbers:
• Full year: revenue ¥108.0B, gross margin 19.0%, operating margin 4.0%
• H1 (Aug–Jan): ¥55.0B = Q1 ¥26.0B + Q2 ¥29.0B (Nov ¥8.6B / Dec ¥11.2B / Jan ¥9.2B)
• About 300,000 PCs for the year, 75,000 in Q1
H1 closes 31 Jan, so the 半期決算セール is our last lever. Please read it before the next sync.

replies.author: prince
replies.text: Thank you. Note the phasing: Q2 is ¥29.0B and December alone is ¥11.2B, so H1 depends heavily on Black Friday and the New Year. I'll set up the monthly tracking sheet against this.

replies.author: jacob
replies.text: Q2 = Black Friday + 初売り + 半期決算セール. Challenge accepted 🔥

replies.author: daniel
replies.text: 300k units is roughly 600k DIMMs a year at our current memory mix. I'll rebuild the parts plan on the new budget and show it in the S&OP.

replies.author: karthi
replies.text: Thanks. One rule for this term: when we're off plan, we say it early, with a 対策.

replies.author: prince
replies.text: Understood 🙇

posts.author: jacob
posts.text: Competitor watch: MCJ (Mouse / G-Tune) is fully private since the June delisting. Their stated focus is mini PCs and gaming. With no quarterly results to report, I expect G-Tune to be more aggressive on price this winter. FRONTIER also never brought prices back down after its +16–41% rise last December.

replies.author: prince
replies.text: MCJ passed most of its costs through last year and still made record profit. I doubt they'll start a price war, but it's worth watching weekly.

replies.author: karthi
replies.text: Jacob, can you add a competitor line to the price committee pack every two weeks? Just price moves on comparable RTX 5070 / 5080 configs.

replies.author: jacob
replies.text: Will do 👍

posts.author: prince
posts.text: FX note: USD/JPY was about ¥159.5 yesterday vs our ¥156 budget rate. Rule of thumb: a ¥5 move ≈ 3% on parts cost. Not dangerous yet, but if we drift back toward the July high (≈ ¥164), Q2 margins get tight.

replies.author: karthi
replies.text: Who owns the hedge question, us or Finance?

replies.author: prince
replies.text: Treasury executes, but they will ask us for the purchase volumes. I'll keep an FX line in the landing file and flag it if we cross ¥160.

replies.author: daniel
replies.text: Memory and GPUs are all USD-priced. I'll share the Q4 and Q1 purchase forecasts with you once Sarah has the contract timing.

posts.author: karthi
posts.text:
Business Planning Charter v4 is up. Main changes:
1. Decision rights: any commitment above ¥100M or any price change needs my sign-off and goes to Robert before the Monthly Management Meeting.
2. Thread first: post the 資料 here before every meeting. Drafts are fine, just put "draft" in the file name.
3. Planning sync stays every other Tuesday 10:00–11:00, plus decision meetings when needed.
Please read it and react when done.

posts.author: prince
posts.text:
Store & Digital Dock plan for FY2027/7 is attached (draft with Retail). Two options:
A) 3 new Dospara stores (≈ ¥150M each incl. fit-out) + 6 new Digital Docks inside existing stores
B) Freeze new stores this year and do only the 6 Digital Docks
My view: repair and support subscriptions are counter-cyclical. People keep old PCs longer when new ones are expensive. New stores are harder to justify while PC units are down.

replies.author: jacob
replies.text: Stores still matter for first-time buyers and for the GALLERIA experience. I'd keep at least one new store in a gaming-heavy area.

replies.author: daniel
replies.text: Supply side: no parts constraint on either option. Digital Dock needs some repair-parts stock, but it's small.

replies.author: karthi
replies.text: Each new store is ≈ ¥150M, so above the ¥100M line; it goes to Robert anyway. Prince, please add a payback period per store and per Digital Dock.

replies.author: prince
replies.text: Understood. I'll add payback and a downside case.

posts.author: daniel
posts.text: Memory news: TrendForce's new forecast (30 Sep) says PC DRAM contract prices +13–18% in Oct–Dec. The rise is slowing because PC sales are weak and OEM stock is high. The bigger point: Korean suppliers plan to cut PC DRAM output by more than 20% in 2027 to favour server DRAM. Prices may calm down; availability may not. Allocation first 🙏

replies.author: prince
replies.text: "Slowing" matters for the over-buying risk. If prices flatten, holding too much stock gets expensive.

replies.author: daniel
replies.text: Agreed on cost. But if the allocation is cut, we can't buy at any price. That's what happened last December.

replies.author: jacob
replies.text: Please, no repeat of last winter. Our ¥119,800 32GB×2 kit in February was national news. The community still jokes about it.

replies.author: karthi
replies.text: Both fair points. Daniel, please get an early read on the Q1 2027 contract with Sarah so November doesn't surprise us.

replies.author: daniel
replies.text: Will do.

posts.author: jacob
posts.text: Black Friday early thinking, before I write the plan: I want ONE simple headline. Proposal: the 16GB → 32GB memory upgrade for +¥9,696, in the early-bird sale (30 Oct–13 Nov) and the main sale (13 Nov 11:00 – 4 Dec 10:59). Gamers look at memory before anything else right now. Thoughts?

replies.author: prince
replies.text: May I raise one concern: the extra 16GB costs us much more than ¥9,696 now. Let me calculate it properly, but if memory keeps rising, every upgrade loses money.

replies.author: jacob
replies.text: I know, but it's the one thing people compare across BTO sites. It's our value message.

replies.author: daniel
replies.text: A high take rate also pulls DRAM faster. Please give me a take-rate assumption so I can check coverage.

replies.author: jacob
replies.text: Plan 60%. Could be higher.

replies.author: karthi
replies.text: Write it into the plan with Prince's cost number next to it. We decide at the 20 Oct kickoff.

replies.author: daniel
replies.text: Thank you.
